newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police arrest six CRB officials.
newsitem.headline: Indian police arrest six CRB officials.

text.p: India's federal police agency said on Thursday it had arrested six people connected with the failed CRB group of companies, accused of irregularities in financial services.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said in a statement it had arrested four directors of CRB group companies, a finance controller of the group and a close associate of CRB chairman Chain Roop Bhansali.
Bhansali was still untraced, a CBI spokesman said. The agency did not say when the arrests were made.
The CBI raided 16 houses and offices of people connected with the group, and seized shares and "incriminating files and other documents", the statement said.
Last week the CBI said it would complete within a month an investigation into the group, whose liabilities are estimated at 9.32 billion rupees ($260 million).

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Wednesday called for tighter regulatory controls over finance firms after the group's flagship, CRB Capital Markets Ltd, was charged with financial irregularities.
Gujral also asked the Finance Ministry to devise a depositors insurance scheme to protect investors in the future.
The Reserve Bank of India, the central bank, last month charged CRB Capital Markets, which has offices in India and abroad, with a series of irregularities relating to its activities.

The bank also invited claims from investors of CRB Capital Markets for submission to the official liquidator appointed by the Delhi High Court. A winding up petition filed by the Reserve Bank of India will be heard on July 22.

The State Bank of India had lodged a complaint with the CBI against the company after it discovered the firm was defaulting on repayments and had withdrawn 580 million rupees on a loan facility, the government said on Wednesday. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
